players.product: AI/automotive chip designer - Samsung Foundry contract-manufacturing customer (USD 16.5B, 2025-2033)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Vaibhav Taneja: 'we are in a very big capital investment phase, which is going to start now and would last a couple of years. Based on that, our current expectation for 2026 is over $25 billion of CapEx.' Tesla is paying for six factories, increasing investment in AI-related initiatives (AI infrastructure for Robotaxi, Optimus launch), and has 'already started placing orders for the research semiconductor fab in Austin and for solar manufacturing equipment.' Q1 free cash flow was just over $1.4 billion; negative free cash flow expected for the rest of the year. Spend on AI initiatives including development of Tesla's own AI5 chip expected to stay elevated for full-year 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: over $25 billion of CapEx (2026 expectation); Q1 free cash flow just over $1.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Research fab (Terafab near-term step): Musk: 'In the near term, Tesla will be building the research fab on our Giga Texas campus. This is something we expect to be probably a $3 billion-ish initiative, and capable of maybe a few thousand wafers per month.' Construction starts this year. Taneja: 'we plan to do memory, logic, everything in the same place, including mask'; Musk: lithography mask creation, logic, memory and packaging 'under one roof in one building' to test new chip-making ideas and production-process soundness.
quarterly_data.figure: $3 billion-ish initiative; maybe a few thousand wafers per month

quarterly_data.signal: Terafab process technology: Musk: 'Intel is excited to partner with us on some of the core manufacturing technologies. We plan to use Intel's 14A process, which is state-of-the-art and in fact, not yet totally complete. Given that by the time Terafab scales up, 14A will be probably fairly mature or ready for prime time, 14A seems like the right move.' Ownership split so far: Tesla does the research fab, SpaceX does the initial phase of the scaled-up Terafab; rest still being worked out (intra-company deals need both boards' approval).
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (Intel 14A process planned for Terafab)

quarterly_data.signal: Why Terafab (supply, not leverage): Musk: 'Terafab is not some sort of mechanism to generate leverage over our chip suppliers. It's just literally we don't see a path to having enough sufficient quantity of AI chips down the road as we scale production to high levels. Just the rate at which the industry is growing, in logic but even more so in memory, we just anticipate hitting the wall if we don't make chips ourselves.' Long term, for AI satellites, 'there's just no way in hell the existing industry can keep up with that.'

AI chip roadmap: the Tesla AI chip team taped out AI5 early (worked every weekend for six months). Musk expects 'AI5 will go into Optimus and into the data center', since unsupervised self-driving looks achievable on AI4, so AI5 is 'certainly not immediately needed in the car.' Design momentum on AI6; discussions begun on ideas for Dojo 3.
quarterly_data.figure: no specific figure (AI5 taped out; AI6 in design)

quarterly_data.signal: AI4 upgrade (AI4.1 / AI4+): Musk: 'We are planning an AI4 upgrade to use a newer generation RAM. It'll go from 16 gigabytes to, I think, 32 gigabytes per SoC, so a total of 64 gigabytes. Probably a 10% increase in compute in trillions of operations per second and in memory bandwidth.' It 'probably goes into production middle of next year'; 'Samsung's doing the modifications for us, so it sort of depends on when they're able to finish those modifications and bring it to production.'
quarterly_data.figure: RAM from 16 gigabytes to 32 gigabytes per SoC (a total of 64 gigabytes); probably a 10% increase in compute

quarterly_data.signal: Memory bandwidth as the AI choke point: Musk: Hardware 3 cannot achieve unsupervised FSD because 'it has only 1/8 of the memory bandwidth of Hardware 4... If you're doing an autoregressive transformer, memory bandwidth is the choke point.' Tesla plans discounted trade-ins and computer + camera retrofits to Hardware 4 via micro factories in major metropolitan areas; a distilled V14 for Hardware 3 expected end of June (Ashok Elluswamy).
quarterly_data.figure: Hardware 3 has 1/8 of the memory bandwidth of Hardware 4

quarterly_data.signal: Energy storage: 'In Q1, we deployed 8.8 GWh of energy storage, a 38% sequential decline', but 2026 deployments still expected higher than 2025. Record energy gross margins over 39.5% helped by more than $250 million of one-time tariff recognitions; normalized margin compression expected from competition and tariffs ('most of the battery cells are procured from China'). Order backlog 'robust'. Musk: 'Demand for our Megapack is very strong'; Megapack 3 production to begin later this year in the new factory outside Houston.
quarterly_data.figure: 8.8 GWh deployed in Q1, a 38% sequential decline; energy gross margins over 39.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 operating color: auto margins excluding credits improved sequentially from 17.9%-19.2%, with one-time benefits from warranty write-downs around $230 million and some relief on tariffs; FSD reached nearly 1.3 million paid customers globally; Giga Berlin record output of over 61,000 units; highest Q1 order backlog in over two years. 'Our biggest limiter continues to be our battery pack capacity' (not cells) - capacity being added via in-house 4680 packs in Berlin, Reno retooling and LFP module production in China. Cybercab production just started; Optimus production at Fremont assumed around late July/August; second Optimus factory at Giga Texas probably starting around summer next year.
quarterly_data.figure: auto margins excluding credits improved sequentially from 17.9%-19.2%; nearly 1.3 million paid customers (FSD); over 61,000 units (Giga Berlin Q1)
